items.stem: Within which scope does Kafka guarantee message ordering?

options.rationale: Correct: ordering is guaranteed per partition, not across a whole topic.

options.text: Across all partitions of a topic
options.rationale: There is no global cross-partition ordering guarantee.

options.text: Across all topics in a cluster
Only when there is exactly one consumer
options.rationale: Consumer count does not change the per-partition ordering guarantee.

items.stem: Which settings help a Kafka producer avoid data loss and duplicates? (Select TWO)

options.text: acks=all so the leader waits for in-sync replicas
options.rationale: Correct: acks=all maximises durability against broker failure.
Correct: idempotence prevents duplicate records from retries.
acks=0 gives no delivery guarantee and risks loss.

options.text: Disabling replication to speed up writes
options.rationale: Removing replication reduces durability, increasing loss risk.

items.stem: What happens if a consumer group has more consumers than a topic has partitions?

options.text: Some consumers sit idle because each partition is assigned to at most one consumer in the group
options.rationale: Correct: parallelism is capped by partition count within a group.

options.text: Every consumer reads every partition in parallel
options.rationale: A partition is assigned to only one consumer per group.

options.text: The extra consumers increase per-partition throughput
options.rationale: They cannot; partition count is the ceiling.

options.text: Kafka automatically splits partitions to match
options.rationale: Partitions are not auto-split to add consumers.

items.explanation: Correct: parallelism is capped by partition count within a group.
